description.summary: application menus in GemWM's menu bar

protocol.description:
In GEM the menu bar belonged to the application in front. This protocol lets a window put its own menus there: while it has focus, GemWM's menu bar shows Desk, a menu for the window, the window's own menus, and Options. A menu the application calls "Options" is merged into GemWM's, above its items.
Menus are sent whole: requests between two commits describe every menu, in order, and commit replaces what was shown. When the user picks an item, the activate event names it. Since version 2 a menu can have submenus, which open to the side, as GEM's did from AES 3.30.

request.name: get_app_menu
request.description: Create the menus object for a toplevel's surface. It has no menus until the first commit.

request.name: menu
request.description: Items and separators after this go in a menu with this title.

request.name: item

description.summary: add an item to the current menu

request.description: The id comes back in activate. The shortcut is only shown, to the right of the label (e.g. "^T"); the application handles the keys itself. It may be empty.

description.summary: add a separator to the current menu

request.name: commit
request.description: The menus sent since the last commit replace the window's menus. A commit with none removes them.

request.name: submenu

description.summary: start a submenu in the current menu

request.description: An entry with this label, opening to the side; items, separators and submenus after this go in it, until end_submenu. Submenus may nest. One with no items is shown disabled.

request.name: end_submenu
request.description: What follows goes back in the menu (or submenu) the submenu is in.
